pageProps.title: The Three-Body Problem 1: The Three-Body Problem
pageProps.review: A review of Liu Cixin's sci-fi novel 'The Three-Body Problem,' where scattered clues set against the collapse of basic physics and a virtual game world connect into a massive narrative, delivering overwhelming immersion.
pageProps.description: It is impossible for humanity to win this war. You are bugs!
pageProps.content:
## Review I really enjoyed reading this. I'm not a fast reader, but I finished this thick book in no time.
The collapse of basic physics as we know it and the resulting suicides of scientists in the early part of the book, along with stories jumping between the past and present and a mysterious virtual game world... these elements are scattered at first. Up to that point, I couldn't tell what the main story was.
However, as I reached the middle, everything started to connect. The concept of the Three-body problem was particularly impressive.
I was so curious about what happens next that I immediately started the next book in the series.
